details: The cryptocurrency market has experienced a significant downturn, with Bitcoin dropping below $67,000, reaching its lowest level since April. This decline is largely attributed to escalating geopolitical concerns surrounding Iran and continued outflows from spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). The market saw over $1 billion in crypto liquidations within hours, marking the largest single-session wipeout since February. Solana also recorded notable price reductions.
title: Crypto Market Plunges Amid Geopolitical Tensions & Outflows

details: The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned Iran's largest crypto exchange, Nobitex, along with Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex. This action, part of an "Economic Fury" campaign, targets entities accused of sanctions evasion, terrorist financing, and supporting the Iranian regime. Nobitex alone was responsible for over 50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025.
title: US Sanctions Major Iranian Crypto Exchanges

details: MicroStrategy Inc., a major corporate holder of Bitcoin, sold 32 BTC for $2.5 million. Although a small fraction of its extensive holdings, this marks the company's first reported net reduction in Bitcoin since 2022. The sale, intended to fund distributions on its perpetual preferred stock, rattled market sentiment, as it deviated from Chairman Michael Saylor's long-standing "never sell" stance and contributed to the broader market sell-off.
title: MicroStrategy's Bitcoin Sale Impacts Market Sentiment

details: The defunct Mt. Gox exchange transferred approximately 10,422 Bitcoin, valued at about $739 million, to new wallets on June 2nd. This significant on-chain movement is its largest in months and has raised concerns among market participants about potential selling pressure as the October 31, 2026, deadline for creditor repayments approaches. Mt. Gox still holds roughly 34,504 BTC.
title: Mt. Gox Moves $739M in BTC Ahead of Repayment

details: The native token of The Open Network (TON), previously Toncoin, is being rebranded to its original name, "Gram." This strategic move is part of Telegram founder Pavel Durov's initiative to integrate the blockchain more deeply with the messaging application, aiming to onboard Telegram's 900 million users into the on-chain ecosystem. The rebranding is primarily a cosmetic change, without any underlying technical modifications to the token.
title: TON Rebrands to 'Gram' Amidst Telegram Integration Push

details: Microsoft unveiled its Majorana 2 quantum chip, claiming it to be 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor. This advancement accelerates the prospect of scalable quantum computing, rekindling long-term concerns about "Q-Day." This is the theoretical point at which powerful quantum computers could compromise the cryptographic security of Bitcoin and other blockchain networks, potentially putting billions in digital assets at risk.
title: Microsoft Quantum Chip Progress Raises Long-Term Crypto Security Concerns
